summary.plain: IceCube reported 28 high-energy neutrino events that interact inside the detector. The collaboration says a purely atmospheric origin is rejected for these events at the 4σ level, and that their properties are consistent with generic predictions for an additional component of extraterrestrial origin.
summary.technical: All-sky search for high-energy neutrino interactions starting inside the detector, May 2010 – May 2012. Twenty-eight events with deposited energies between 30 and 1200 TeV reject a purely atmospheric origin at 4σ; their flavours, directions and energies are inconsistent with the atmospheric muon and neutrino backgrounds and consistent with generic predictions for an additional component of extraterrestrial origin.

title: Evidence for High-Energy Extraterrestrial Neutrinos at the IceCube Detector
why_it_matters: The abstract says the twenty-eight events include the highest energy neutrinos ever observed and have flavors, directions and energies inconsistent with those expected from atmospheric muon and neutrino backgrounds, while being consistent with generic predictions for an additional component of extraterrestrial origin.
